solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A couple of quarts necked by N Hull CID sneakily around one?

indicators.note: to neck a drink is to swallow it, so the quarts disappear inside the other letters
the scrambled police letters sit around the single letter for one
acting sneakily means moving about by hidden routes, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for quart, here doubled as quarts
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Hull detective downs a pint or two on the sly while on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of N HULL CID ('sneakily') goes 'around' I, and QU is 'necked by' it, swallowed inside. To 'have a couple' is to have a few drinks; read on, 'A couple of quarts necked' extends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a couple means having a few drinks, and a midday meal taken mostly as alcohol is exactly that.

clue.text: Destiny of clergy when leaving the church?

indicators.note: the church is said to be leaving, so its letters go out of the word for clergy

parts.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy
CH is a standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A question about what becomes of priests who quit the church.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's fate or portion, a synonym of destiny.

clue.text: Missing element of DESSTS or AFTS?

definitions.text: Missing element of DESSTS or AFTS?

parts.words: Missing element of DESSTS or AFTS?
parts.note: DESSERTS and AFTERS, both words for puddings, have each lost ER, the abbreviation for the monarch Elizabeth Regina, so what is missing is the royal lady of the puddings

explanation.surface: A puzzle about two misspelt words on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword queen; take it out of DESSERTS and AFTERS and you get the clue's stumps. AFTERS is British slang for the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional British baked pudding of breadcrumbs, jam and meringue, whose name the clue reads literally as the royal missing from pudding words.

clue.text: Cup-tie abandoned, dropping temperature causing freeze

indicators.note: an abandoned match is in disarray, so these letters are rearranged
the letter for temperature is dropped from the words for the match

explanation.surface: A football cup match is called off when the thermometer plunges and the pitch freezes.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup-tie is a knockout match in a British football competition. Taking T from CUPTIE leaves CUPIE, which 'abandoned' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become covered or blocked with ice, which is to freeze over.

clue.text: One needs breather before one winds this to make garment

indicators.note: the breather comes before the one in the finished word

parts.note: a lung is the organ you breathe with
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone needs a breath before wrapping themselves in a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest, but it is the organ. 'One winds this to make garment' tells you the cloth is wrapped round the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Draw up ace duty list for people to flog swimming pools

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawing the pieces up means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the same as ace, and is written AI
a rota is a list of who does which duty when
to tan someone is to give them a beating

explanation.surface: A manager draws up a staff rota of pool attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatoria is the Latin plural of natatorium, an indoor swimming bath.

clue.text: Show where ship's cargo's put on river

parts.note: the hold is the storage space below a ship's deck
the Forth is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A display of where a vessel's goods are stowed, on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth is the Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense to hold forth is to offer or put forward to view, so to exhibit or show.

clue.text: Uninspiring crossword compiler? She's core

parts.note: a setter calls themself me

indicators.note: the core of the word she is its centre letter, so only the middle is taken

explanation.surface: A dull crossword setter who is really a woman at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Meh is a shrugging interjection used as an adjective for something boring or mediocre.

clue.text: Are they first observed by MCC?

definitions.text: Are they first observed by MCC?

parts.words: Are they first observed by MCC?
parts.note: a batsman's first scores of a hundred runs, which the Marylebone Cricket Club, cricket's old governing body, might watch at Lord's; MCC also starts with M then C for maiden and century

explanation.surface: A question about what the cricket authorities see first.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, based at Lord's in London. 'first' hints at maiden; M and C are also the opening letters of the two words, with C the abbreviation for a century.
explanation.definitionFit: A player's maiden hundred is their first score of a hundred runs in an innings, observed first by anyone watching.

clue.text: One does cut luxurious German cheese, does one?

parts.note: high living is luxurious living

indicators.note: the letter for one is said to cut the cheese, going into it

parts.note: Tilsit is a semi-hard cheese named after the former Prussian town
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A posh person slices fancy German cheese, or so it asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do one' is British slang for go away, leave quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hightail it is American slang for leaving in a hurry, matching the British slang for clearing off.

clue.text: I'm not allowed to say who knows

definitions.meaning: a refusal to reveal something you are bound to keep secret
a shrug meaning the outcome is impossible to predict

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean a secret will not be told, or that nobody can forecast what happens.

clue.text: Signatory should first look at this splendid beer, brewer's last bottled

definitions.text: Signatory should first look at this

parts.note: fine means excellent or splendid

indicators.note: the brewer's last letter is put inside the beer, as if bottled in it

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer

indicators.note: only the final letter of the brewer is wanted here

explanation.surface: Advice to someone signing up to a splendid beer deal from a brewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The small-print terms and conditions of a contract are what anyone signing should read first.

clue.text: Like young pack member growing up, one must pay 60s cult

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cub is pre-wolf, not yet a grown member of the pack
an ower is one who owes money

explanation.surface: A Cub Scout grows up and joins a sixties cult, at a price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young pack member' suggests a Cub Scout; here it is a wolf cub, cryptically PRE-WOLF, which 'growing up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippie movement of the 1960s, preaching peace and love with flowers as its symbol.

clue.text: Navy sheltered herein?

indicators.note: the question mark asks the solver to read herein as here in, so the shelter word goes inside this paper's initials

parts.note: here, for a solver of this puzzle, is the Financial Times, abbreviated FT
the lee side is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Is a navy's harbour a place where ships are sheltered?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'herein' as 'here in': 'here' is this paper, the Financial Times, and 'in' puts the sheltered side inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a country's whole force of warships, so a synonym for its navy.

clue.text: Green about the gills, not in the pink?

definitions.meaning: read literally, not of the right shade, wrongly tinted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unwell, and also playfully names something of the wrong shade, since in the pink means healthy.

clue.text: Flanker is in flight

definitions.meaning: a flanker in rugby is a wing forward, playing out wide
flying through the air, as a bird does

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, flankers are also called wing forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes where a wide player is positioned and also a bird flying.

clue.text: Love new-style earrings? I'll order!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: the earrings are given a new style, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic shopper loves a new design of earrings and places an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts things in order, or arranges events, organises them.

clue.text: Behind games area it flexes muscles

indicators.note: the turned-round word comes behind the games area

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public sports field

indicators.note: flexing bends, so the little word is turned back on itself

explanation.surface: Someone at the back of the playing field shows off their muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British recreation ground, a public park for games.
explanation.definitionFit: Recti is the Latin plural of rectus, a name for several straight muscles such as the abdominals.

clue.text: Vent sudden anger, Virgin having backtracked — then fall out of train

indicators.note: going back along a track means the word for virgin is read backwards

parts.note: pure means chaste or virgin

indicators.note: the fall is taken out of the word train

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A furious Virgin rail passenger after the train reversed and they stepped off.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin Trains was a British rail operator, hence the train imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out suddenly with anger, as a volcano bursts out.

clue.text: Warmly welcomes employees at stable and farm, joining general staff

indicators.note: the workers join the staff, entering inside its letters

parts.note: GS is the military abbreviation for general staff
a stable lad works in a racing stable
a farm hand is a labourer on a farm

explanation.surface: A staff manager greets new stable and farm workers joining the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employees' serves both workplaces: a stable worker and a farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To glad-hand is to greet people effusively, often insincerely, as politicians do.

clue.text: Living accommodation connected to priest's address

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's flat or home
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A home attached to a clergyman's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a house location; it is the way one speaks to a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is how one addresses a chaplain or priest, from the Spanish and Italian for father.

clue.text: Arithmetic: two poor grades in ten? Turning that round, it's essential!

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is then turned round and read backwards
the sums and grades go inside the word ten

parts.note: sums are arithmetic exercises
D and E are low marks in an exam grading

explanation.surface: A pupil's maths report: two bad marks out of ten, but it's a must to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ten' puts SUMSDE inside TEN, making TSUMSDEEN, which 'Turning that round' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says something must be done because circumstances require it, so it is unavoidable.

clue.text: Exceptionally wide?

definitions.meaning: very or unusually, as in especially large
in cricket a wide is a run conceded for a ball bowled out of reach, a kind of bonus run

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs not scored off the bat, such as wides and byes, are classed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unusually, and is also the cricket category that includes a wide.

clue.text: Quiet little street in which you may witness a scrap

indicators.note: the a is seen inside the quiet street

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
RD is a short form of road

explanation.surface: A quiet side street where you might see a fight break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight; it is a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken fragment of glass or pottery, a small scrap.

clue.text: I was out of order with union 'nitwit' (finishing up in it either way?)

definitions.text: finishing up in it either way?

indicators.note: letters out of order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade union member admits being rude to a colleague he called a nitwit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending up 'in it', such as a winning position, whichever way things go describes an outcome good for both sides.

clue.text: Dreamland, is it — or "reamlan"?

parts.note: the clue's made-up word is the word Dreamland with ... at all

explanation.surface: A question about whether a strange word is the land of dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Ds from DREAMLAND to get REAMLAN: it is Dreamland with no D.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of Nod is the proverbial land of sleep, from the Bible's land east of Eden.

clue.text: Not entirely foolhardy African prince

indicators.note: the word for foolhardy is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: rash means recklessly bold

explanation.surface: An African prince who is a bit reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince or duke, as in Ras Tafari.

clue.text: Scarlet dresses one in department store took in eagerly!

indicators.note: the bloodied word dresses, or wraps around, the store

parts.note: gored means bloodied, so scarlet with blood

indicators.note: the one goes inside the department store

parts.note: M and S is Marks and Spencer, the British department store chain
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman in a red dress is spotted in Marks and Spencer, grabbing goods.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S (Marks and Spencer) is a British high-street department store; 'Scarlet' is bloodied, not merely red.
explanation.definitionFit: To gormandise is to eat greedily, devouring food like a glutton.
